sentence: Bond enthalpies provide an estimate of reaction enthalpy by treating the process as breaking all the bonds in the reactants and forming all the bonds in the products. The reaction enthalpy approximates the sum of bond enthalpies broken minus the sum of bond enthalpies formed, although the values are averages and the estimate carries an uncertainty of tens of kilojoules.

Aqueous-phase organic synthesis benefits from hydrophobic interactions that accelerate Diels-Alder and aldol reactions through enforced reactant proximity. Breslow demonstrated rate enhancements of two orders of magnitude for cyclopentadiene plus methyl vinyl ketone in water versus organic solvent. Surfactant-formed micelles can extend the approach to water-insoluble substrates, hosting reactants in their hydrophobic cores.

The standard enthalpy of formation is the enthalpy change when one mole of a compound forms from its elements in their reference states. The enthalpy of any reaction equals the sum of the formation enthalpies of the products minus that of the reactants, since the elemental reference states cancel and define the zero of the formation scale.

Potentiometric titration follows the change in indicator electrode potential, often a glass electrode for acid-base reactions or a metal electrode for redox titrations, as titrant is added. The equivalence point appears as a steep inflection in the curve. The Nernst equation describes the electrode response: E = E_0 + (RT/nF) ln([Ox]/[Red]).

Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy exploits the Zeeman splitting of nuclear spin states in an external magnetic field. Hydrogen-1 in an organic molecule resonates at slightly different frequencies depending on its electronic environment, giving the chemical shift in parts per million. Spin-spin coupling between neighbouring protons produces multiplet patterns whose splittings reveal connectivity.

Atropisomerism is a form of chirality arising from restricted rotation about a single bond rather than from a stereocentre. In biphenyls bearing bulky ortho substituents the two rings cannot become coplanar, freezing the molecule into a twisted shape that exists as separable enantiomeric conformers. The barrier to interconversion must exceed about 90 kilojoules per mole for the atropisomers to be isolable at room temperature.

X-ray crystallography determines atomic positions by interpreting the diffraction pattern produced when X-rays scatter from a crystalline lattice. The Bragg condition 2 d sin theta = n lambda relates the angle of diffraction maxima to interplanar spacings. Phase information, lost in measured intensities, is recovered through direct methods, isomorphous replacement, or molecular replacement.

Ring expansion of a strained cyclic carbocation relieves angle strain by migration of a ring bond to the cationic carbon. A cyclobutylmethyl cation rearranges to the less strained cyclopentyl cation, and a cyclopropylcarbinyl cation enjoys special stabilisation through donation from the bent ring bonds before ring-opening to a homoallyl product.

Intramolecular hydrogen bonding can override the intermolecular variety. Ortho-nitrophenol forms an internal hydrogen bond between its hydroxyl and nitro groups, so it has little capacity left to bond with neighbours and is steam-volatile, whereas para-nitrophenol bonds extensively between molecules, raising its melting point and lowering its volatility markedly.

Alcoholic fermentation by Saccharomyces cerevisiae converts glucose to ethanol and carbon dioxide through the Embden-Meyerhof-Parnas pathway followed by pyruvate decarboxylation and reduction of acetaldehyde. Theoretical yield is 0.51 grams ethanol per gram glucose; in practice 0.46 is achieved, with the remainder lost to glycerol, organic acids, and biomass production. Higher alcohols and esters generated as fermentation byproducts at the milligram per litre level define the flavour profile of wine and beer.

The inert pair effect explains why the heavier p-block elements favour an oxidation state two below the group maximum. Lead is far more stable as plus two than plus four, and bismuth as plus three rather than plus five, because the 6s electrons are poorly shielded, contracted by relativistic effects, and reluctant to participate in bonding.

Prochirality describes a centre that becomes a stereocentre upon a single substitution. The two hydrogens on the methylene carbon of ethanol are enantiotopic, indistinguishable in an achiral environment but distinguished by an enzyme. Alcohol dehydrogenase removes specifically the pro-R hydrogen, demonstrating that biological catalysts can select between groups that are equivalent to ordinary reagents.

Squalene, a thirty-carbon triterpene, is formed by reductive tail-to-tail coupling of two molecules of farnesyl pyrophosphate. Its enzymatic epoxidation gives 2,3-oxidosqualene, which undergoes a remarkable cation-driven polycyclisation cascade that forms four rings in a single concerted sequence, the biosynthetic origin of lanosterol and ultimately of cholesterol.

Quantum dots of cadmium selenide synthesised by hot injection of selenium precursor into trioctylphosphine oxide containing cadmium oleate yield monodisperse nanocrystals 2 to 8 nanometres in diameter. Their emission tunes from 480 to 640 nanometres through quantum confinement: smaller dots have wider band gap. Capping with a wider-gap ZnS shell raises photoluminescence quantum yield above 80 percent by passivating surface dangling bonds.

Electron capture occurs when a proton-rich nucleus absorbs an inner-shell electron, converting a proton to a neutron and emitting a neutrino. The vacancy left in the electron shell is filled from above, releasing a characteristic X-ray. Potassium-40 decays partly by this route to argon-40, the basis of potassium-argon dating of volcanic rocks.

Templated metal-ligand self-assembly produces discrete polyhedra and capsules from simple subunits. Fujita's M6L4 octahedra form quantitatively when three bidentate pyridyl ligands meet at each square-planar Pd(II) vertex. The internal cavity of roughly one cubic nanometre accommodates four molecules of adamantane, and confinement of reactive guests inside catalyses cycloaddition and Diels-Alder reactions with rate accelerations of several orders of magnitude.

Glucose exists in solution as an equilibrium mixture of cyclic hemiacetal forms. The open-chain aldehyde closes when the C5 hydroxyl attacks the carbonyl, creating a new stereocentre at C1 called the anomeric carbon. The alpha and beta anomers, differing only in the orientation of the anomeric hydroxyl, interconvert through the open chain in the process of mutarotation.

Salts whose constituent ions hydrolyse can be more soluble in acid than the solubility product alone would suggest. Calcium fluoride dissolves more readily in acidic solution because protons consume fluoride as hydrofluoric acid, depleting the free fluoride concentration and dragging the dissolution equilibrium forward until the buffered acid is exhausted.

Cytochrome P450 enzymes oxidise drug molecules at the soft electrophilic positions through an iron-oxo intermediate, hydroxylating allylic and benzylic carbons, dealkylating N-methyl and O-methyl groups, and epoxidising electron-rich alkenes. CYP3A4 metabolises roughly half of marketed drugs, and inhibitors such as ketoconazole or grapefruit juice furanocoumarins raise plasma concentrations of co-administered substrates, often producing clinically important interactions.

The polarity of a solvent, expressed through its dielectric constant, governs what it dissolves. Water with a dielectric constant near 80 screens ionic charges effectively and dissolves salts, while hexane with a dielectric constant near 2 dissolves only non-polar substances, the empirical rule that like dissolves like resting on the matching of intermolecular force types.

Ziegler-Natta catalysts based on TiCl4 and triethylaluminium polymerise propylene to isotactic polypropylene with high stereoregularity. The active titanium centre coordinates the alkene face-selectively, and the alkyl migrates to give a new metal-carbon bond with consistent stereochemistry. The resulting crystalline polymer melts near 165 degrees Celsius, in contrast to atactic polypropylene which is a tacky amorphous material below 0 degrees.

Enzyme catalysis lowers the activation barrier by stabilising the transition state more than the substrate, increasing the rate by factors that can exceed ten orders of magnitude. The catalytic proficiency, defined as the ratio kcat over Km divided by the uncatalysed rate constant, measures how tightly the enzyme binds the transition-state structure relative to the ground-state substrate.

Solvent polarity shifts the position of tautomeric and conformational equilibria. The enol content of a 1,3-dicarbonyl compound rises in non-polar solvents that favour the intramolecularly hydrogen-bonded enol and falls in polar solvents that compete for the carbonyl oxygens and stabilise the more polar diketo form instead.

Nylon-6,6 is synthesised by condensation of hexamethylenediamine with adipic acid, with elimination of water at each amide bond formation. The intermediate nylon salt is heated under pressure to drive equilibrium toward high molecular weight. Carothers' equation gives the number-average degree of polymerisation as X_n = 1/(1 - p), where p is the extent of reaction, demanding stoichiometric balance and conversions exceeding 0.99 for usable fibres.

The carbon of methane is sp3 hybridised, four equivalent orbitals formed by mixing one 2s and three 2p orbitals pointing to the corners of a tetrahedron at 109.5 degrees. Each overlaps with a hydrogen 1s orbital to give four identical sigma bonds, explaining why all four carbon-hydrogen bonds in methane are of equal length and strength.

Acid deposition originates with conversion of sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides to sulphuric and nitric acids in the gas and aqueous phases. Rainwater of pH below 5.6 reflects acid loading beyond the natural CO2 equilibrium baseline. Catalysis by transition-metal ions in cloud droplets accelerates the SO2 oxidation pathway, and the deposited acids accelerate weathering of carbonate buildings and acidify poorly buffered lakes and soils.

Naphthalene, anthracene, and phenanthrene are polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons whose fused rings share pi electrons across the framework. The resonance energy per ring falls with increasing linear fusion, so the central ring of anthracene is the most reactive site and readily undergoes Diels-Alder addition across its 9 and 10 positions while the outer rings stay aromatic.

subtopic: peptide bond formation and protecting groups
sentence: Native chemical ligation joins two unprotected peptide fragments by reacting a carboxyl-terminal thioester with an amino-terminal cysteine. A reversible transthioesterification first links the fragments, and a spontaneous intramolecular acyl shift then converts the thioester into a stable peptide bond, enabling the assembly of full-length proteins from synthetic pieces.

Microplastic weathering in the marine environment proceeds through UV-induced chain scission of polyethylene and polypropylene, generating carbonyl groups detectable by FTIR. Brittle photo-oxidised fragments then crack into nanoplastics under wave action. The resulting particles adsorb hydrophobic pollutants from seawater up to a million-fold higher than ambient concentrations, providing a vector for pollutant uptake by filter-feeders that mistake the particles for food.

The nuclear Overhauser effect transfers magnetisation between nuclei close in space through dipolar relaxation, its intensity falling off as the inverse sixth power of internuclear distance. A NOESY spectrum therefore reveals which protons lie within about five angstroms of each other, distinguishing cis from trans alkene geometry and establishing the three-dimensional fold of a peptide.

Schottky defects in an ionic crystal consist of paired vacancies of cations and anions that preserve overall electroneutrality, lowering the density slightly. Frenkel defects instead displace an ion from its lattice site into an interstitial position. The equilibrium defect concentration rises exponentially with temperature according to the formation enthalpy, governing ionic conductivity in solid electrolytes.

An E1 elimination begins with ionisation of the leaving group to form a carbocation, followed by loss of a beta proton by a base. Because the cation is planar, both syn and anti elimination products are observed, and rearrangements via hydride or methyl shifts to more stable carbocations are common. The Zaitsev product, with the more substituted alkene, usually predominates.

Long-range correlations in an HMBC experiment connect protons to carbons two and three bonds away, bridging the gaps left by directly bonded HSQC correlations. A proton showing an HMBC cross-peak to a carbonyl carbon establishes that the proton sits alpha or beta to that carbonyl, knitting together fragments across quaternary carbons and heteroatoms that interrupt the proton-coupled network.

Diborane adopts a structure with two bridging hydrogen atoms held by three-centre two-electron bonds, in which a single pair of electrons binds three atoms across a banana-shaped orbital. The molecule is electron-deficient, having too few valence electrons for ordinary two-centre bonds, which explains its bridged geometry and high reactivity toward Lewis bases.

Persistent organic pollutants such as polychlorinated biphenyls, dioxins, and the legacy pesticide DDT resist biodegradation because of high carbon-chlorine bond strength and steric protection of the aromatic ring. Their octanol-water partition coefficients above 10^6 drive bioaccumulation in fatty tissue. The Stockholm Convention has phased out their production, yet legacy contamination in cold remote regions persists because volatilisation-condensation cycles distil them poleward over decades.

The anti-Markovnikov addition of hydrogen bromide to an alkene proceeds when peroxides are present, switching the mechanism from ionic to radical. A bromine atom adds to the less hindered carbon to give the more stable secondary radical, which then abstracts hydrogen from hydrogen bromide, so the bromine ends up on the less substituted carbon.

The Langmuir adsorption isotherm theta = K p / (1 + K p) assumes a homogeneous surface of identical sites with no lateral interactions between adsorbates and monolayer coverage at saturation. Linearisation as p/V = p/V_m + 1/(K V_m) yields the monolayer capacity V_m and equilibrium constant K from the slope and intercept. The model fails for porous adsorbents where the BET extension is required.

An SN2 reaction proceeds with inversion of configuration because the nucleophile attacks the carbon from the side opposite the leaving group, passing through a trigonal bipyramidal transition state. When the carbon is a stereocentre, this Walden inversion converts an R substrate cleanly into an S product, providing a stereochemical fingerprint that distinguishes the concerted bimolecular mechanism from a racemising SN1 pathway.

Ring-opening metathesis polymerisation of norbornene with Grubbs' second-generation ruthenium catalyst yields polynorbornene with cis-trans olefin ratios tunable through catalyst and temperature. The cyclic strain of norbornene provides the thermodynamic driving force, while the metal alkylidene cycles through metallacyclobutane intermediates. Functional group tolerance extends to esters, alcohols, and even acidic protons, enabling polymerisation of biologically relevant monomers.

Fluorine-18 is a positron-emitting isotope incorporated into tracers for positron emission tomography. The radiolabelled glucose analogue fluorodeoxyglucose accumulates in metabolically active tissue and is trapped after phosphorylation. The short half-life near 110 minutes demands rapid synthesis and prompt imaging once the labelled molecule is prepared.

Radical cyclisation of a hex-5-enyl radical favours the five-membered ring over the six-membered ring, contrary to thermodynamic stability. The Baldwin rules and stereoelectronic analysis of the transition state show that the chair-like arrangement for 5-exo-trig closure aligns the radical with the alkene pi system more effectively than the 6-endo alternative.

The tropylium cation is an aromatic seven-membered ring carrying a single positive charge and six pi electrons delocalised over all seven carbons. Its stability lets it form spontaneously when cycloheptatriene loses hydride, and the aromatic character also explains the prominent mass-spectral fragment at mass-to-charge 91 that arises when benzylic ions rearrange to tropylium.

Boron is electron deficient and forms a remarkable family of cluster hydrides. Diborane has no ordinary two-centre bonds between its borons; instead two bridging hydrogens each form a three-centre two-electron bond spanning two boron atoms and one hydrogen, a bonding motif that resolves the apparent shortage of valence electrons in the molecule.

Beta-hydride elimination from a metal alkyl regenerates a metal hydride and releases an alkene through a four-centre transition state requiring a vacant coordination site syn to the beta-hydrogen. The reaction terminates many polymerisation chains and underlies the Pd-catalysed Wacker oxidation of ethylene to acetaldehyde. Catalyst design that suppresses beta-hydride elimination, as in bulky cone-angle ligand environments, enables longer chain growth.

The Gibbs free energy change Delta G = Delta H - T Delta S determines whether a process is spontaneous at constant temperature and pressure. Reactions with Delta G < 0 proceed in the forward direction, those with Delta G > 0 are nonspontaneous, and Delta G = 0 corresponds to chemical equilibrium. The condition unifies enthalpic and entropic driving forces in a single quantitative criterion.

Azobisisobutyronitrile is a common radical initiator that decomposes on gentle heating, expelling a molecule of nitrogen and releasing two carbon-centred radicals. The loss of stable dinitrogen provides the thermodynamic driving force, and the decomposition rate, with a convenient half-life near ten hours at 65 degrees Celsius, makes the reagent a controllable radical source.

The boron hydrides form an extensive series of cluster compounds whose structures Wade's rules rationalise by counting skeletal electron pairs. A closo cluster with n vertices has n plus one skeletal pairs, a nido cluster has n plus two, and an arachno cluster has n plus three, each successive class derived by stripping a vertex from the parent deltahedron.

Transesterification exchanges the alkoxy group of an ester for that of a different alcohol under acid or base catalysis. The mechanism is the familiar addition-elimination at the acyl carbon, and the equilibrium is shifted by supplying a large excess of the incoming alcohol or by distilling away the more volatile displaced alcohol as it forms.

Nuclear binding energy is the energy released when nucleons assemble into a nucleus, reflected in a mass defect through the mass-energy equivalence. The binding energy per nucleon peaks near iron-56, so fusing light nuclei and splitting heavy ones both release energy, accounting for stellar fusion at one end of the curve and reactor fission at the other.

Mossbauer spectroscopy exploits recoilless gamma emission and absorption by nuclei in solids to resolve hyperfine interactions of typical magnitude 10^-8 electron volts. Iron-57 at 14.4 kiloelectron volts is the most widely used isotope. Isomer shift, quadrupole splitting, and magnetic splitting reported in the spectrum diagnose oxidation state, coordination geometry, and magnetic ordering in iron-containing minerals, proteins, and catalysts.

Hydrophobic effects can accelerate reactions in water by forcing non-polar reactants together to minimise their disruption of the hydrogen-bonded network. Diels-Alder reactions run markedly faster in aqueous suspension than in organic solvents because the diene and dienophile are pressed into proximity, and the polar transition state is further stabilised by water.

The isoprene rule, recognised by Wallach and refined by Ruzicka, observes that terpene carbon skeletons can be divided into isoprene units joined in a regular head-to-tail pattern. The biogenetic isoprene rule extended the idea by proposing that the skeletons arise from cyclisation and rearrangement of a small number of acyclic polyprenyl precursors.

The Bateman equations describe sequential radioactive decay in a chain such as uranium-238 to thorium-234 to protactinium-234 to uranium-234. Secular equilibrium is reached when the parent half-life vastly exceeds the daughter's, giving daughter activity equal to parent activity. Geochemical disequilibria in uranium series isotopes are exploited to date carbonate corals and travertines over the past 500,000 years.

Fischer carbenes have an empty p orbital on carbon stabilised by pi-donation from a heteroatomic substituent and are electrophilic at the carbene carbon. Schrock carbenes lack the heteroatomic stabilisation and are nucleophilic. Both classes participate in olefin metathesis through metallacyclobutane intermediates, but Schrock alkylidenes operate at higher oxidation states with Mo, W, or Ta, while Grubbs' Ru alkylidenes blend characteristics of both.

Amides are the least reactive carboxylic acid derivatives because the nitrogen lone pair is strongly delocalised into the carbonyl, giving the C-N bond substantial double-bond character. Hydrolysis of an amide therefore requires forcing conditions, prolonged heating with strong acid or base, to overcome both the poor electrophilicity and the poor leaving-group ability of the amide nitrogen.

Amylose and amylopectin are the two polymers of starch, both built from alpha-glucose. Amylose is a linear alpha-1,4 chain that coils into a helix and gives the deep blue complex with iodine, while amylopectin carries alpha-1,6 branch points every twenty-odd residues, producing a bushy structure that is rapidly mobilised by enzymes attacking many chain ends at once.

Enzyme catalysis achieves rate accelerations of 10^10 to 10^17 over uncatalysed reactions by preferentially stabilising the transition state. Triose phosphate isomerase approaches the diffusion-controlled limit for proton transfer between dihydroxyacetone phosphate and glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate. The active site precisely positions a glutamate base and a histidine acid relative to the substrate, while exclusion of bulk water raises the effective concentration of catalytic residues.

Fatty acid beta-oxidation in the mitochondrial matrix cleaves two-carbon units from saturated acyl-CoA chains through cycles of dehydrogenation, hydration, second dehydrogenation, and thiolytic cleavage. Each cycle yields one FADH2, one NADH, and one acetyl-CoA, with palmitate fully oxidised to eight acetyl-CoA and supplying roughly 106 ATP equivalents after complete oxidation through the citric acid cycle and oxidative phosphorylation.

Reductive elimination from a d8 square planar Pd(II) complex closes the catalytic cycle of cross-coupling by forming the new C-C or C-heteroatom bond and regenerating the Pd(0) species. The geometry requires cis arrangement of the two coupling partners on Pd. Bulky monodentate phosphines such as t-Bu3P and biphenyl-based dialkylbiarylphosphines accelerate reductive elimination by destabilising the four-coordinate intermediate.

Selective hydrogenation of alkynes to cis-alkenes uses Lindlar's catalyst, palladium poisoned with lead and quinoline on calcium carbonate support. The poisons attenuate Pd activity sufficiently that the more strongly adsorbed alkyne reacts faster than the alkene product, preventing overreduction to alkane. Cis selectivity follows from syn delivery of two hydrogens to the same face of the alkyne while bound to the metal surface.

Neutron activation analysis quantifies trace elements by irradiating a sample with thermal neutrons in a reactor and measuring delayed gamma emissions from the activated nuclides. Sodium-24 with a 15-hour half-life and gold-198 with a 2.7-day half-life are routinely detected at parts per billion levels. The technique is matrix-insensitive, non-destructive in many configurations, and stood out historically in forensic analysis of Napoleon's hair samples for arsenic.

Sol-gel synthesis of silica proceeds by hydrolysis of tetraethyl orthosilicate Si(OEt)4 to silanol intermediates, followed by condensation polymerisation forming Si-O-Si bridges. Acid catalysis favours linear oligomers and gels with small mesopores; base catalysis promotes branched colloidal particles that coalesce into porous monoliths. Supercritical drying with carbon dioxide yields aerogels with porosities above 95 percent and densities as low as 0.003 grams per cubic centimetre.

Benzene's pi system is treated by combining six parallel p orbitals into six delocalised molecular orbitals. Three are bonding and fully occupied by the six pi electrons, satisfying the Huckel count of 4n plus 2 for aromatic stability. The lowest orbital has no nodes, and the degenerate pair above it each carry one node, producing the exceptional thermodynamic stability of the aromatic ring.

A lithium-ion cell shuttles Li+ between a graphite anode and a layered transition-metal oxide cathode such as LiCoO2 across a separator soaked in lithium hexafluorophosphate dissolved in ethylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate. Discharging the cell intercalates Li+ into the oxide while the corresponding electrons traverse the external circuit, delivering nominal cell voltage of 3.7 V at energy density approaching 250 Wh per kilogram.

Graham's law states that the rate of effusion of a gas is inversely proportional to the square root of its molar mass. Hydrogen effuses four times faster than oxygen because the mass ratio is sixteen and its square root is four. The principle was exploited in the gaseous diffusion enrichment of uranium hexafluoride, where the isotopic mass difference is tiny.

Continuous flow chemistry replaces batch reactors with narrow channels through which reagents are pumped at controlled rates. Heat and mass transfer scale favourably with the inverse of channel diameter, enabling fast highly exothermic reactions like diazomethane chemistry to be run at the millimetre scale with millisecond residence times. Hazardous intermediates are generated and consumed in situ without accumulation, reducing the risk envelope by orders of magnitude.

Supercritical carbon dioxide is a tunable solvent for extraction and reaction chemistry whose density and dielectric constant vary continuously above 31 degrees Celsius and 74 bar. Decaffeination of coffee beans by scCO2 leaves no toxic solvent residue and preserves flavour compounds. Polymer foaming, dry cleaning, and asymmetric hydrogenation of prochiral substrates have all been performed in this medium with reduced environmental footprint.

A 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition combines a 1,3-dipole such as an azide with a dipolarophile such as an alkyne to form a five-membered ring. The reaction is a [3+2] process under orbital-symmetry control, and the copper-catalysed version of the azide-alkyne coupling delivers 1,4-disubstituted triazoles regioselectively, the cornerstone reaction of click chemistry.

The Barton-McCombie deoxygenation removes a secondary hydroxyl group through a radical chain. The alcohol is first converted to a thiocarbonyl derivative, a tributyltin radical adds to the thiocarbonyl sulfur, and the resulting carbon radical abstracts hydrogen from tin hydride, replacing the oxygen functionality with hydrogen under mild neutral conditions.

Monoterpene cyclases convert geranyl pyrophosphate into cyclic products by first isomerising it to linalyl pyrophosphate, whose freely rotating bond allows the chain to coil. Ionisation then yields a cyclohexenyl cation that is quenched in different ways, producing limonene, alpha-pinene, or camphene depending on how the enzyme channels the reactive intermediate.

The Maillard reaction begins with condensation of a reducing sugar carbonyl with an amino acid amine to form an N-substituted glycosylamine, which rearranges through the Amadori intermediate. Subsequent dehydration and fragmentation generate hundreds of flavour-active products including furans, pyrazines, and pyrroles, accompanied by polymerisation into brown melanoidin pigments responsible for crust colour in baked bread and roasted coffee.

The E-factor introduced by Sheldon measures the mass of waste per mass of product. Bulk chemicals run with E-factors below 5, fine chemicals 5 to 50, and pharmaceuticals often above 100. The high pharmaceutical figure reflects multi-step syntheses with chromatographic purification at each stage, dilute reactions in organic solvents, and aqueous workups that generate large volumes of contaminated wash water requiring incineration or biological treatment.

Dalton's law of partial pressures states that the total pressure of a gas mixture equals the sum of the pressures each component would exert alone. When a gas is collected over water the measured pressure includes the water vapour pressure, which must be subtracted before applying the ideal gas law to find the moles of the dry gas collected.

Kinetic resolution exploits the unequal reaction rates of two enantiomers with a chiral catalyst or reagent. A lipase that acylates one enantiomer of a racemic alcohol much faster than the other leaves the slow enantiomer unreacted, so partial conversion yields both the enantiopure ester and the enantiopure recovered alcohol at the cost of half the material.

The root mean square speed of gas molecules equals the square root of three RT divided by the molar mass. For nitrogen at room temperature this gives roughly 515 metres per second, close to the speed of sound in air, while a heavier gas such as carbon dioxide moves more slowly under identical conditions because its larger molar mass appears in the denominator.

Asymmetric hydrogenation with Noyori's BINAP-Ru catalysts reduces beta-ketoesters to beta-hydroxyesters with enantiomeric excess above 99 percent. The chiral pocket of the catalyst differentiates the prochiral faces of the substrate through quadrant analysis: bulky aryl groups of BINAP occupy two diagonal quadrants while the substrate orients with its small substituent in the remaining quadrant, dictating which face receives the hydride.

subtopic: peptide bond formation and protecting groups
sentence: The tert-butoxycarbonyl group shields an amine as a carbamate and is removed by treatment with trifluoroacetic acid, which protonates the carbonyl oxygen and triggers loss of a stable tert-butyl cation followed by decarboxylation. Its acid-lability complements the base-labile fluorenylmethyloxycarbonyl group in two-dimensional protection schemes.

Contact angle measurements probe surface energetics through Young's equation gamma_sv = gamma_sl + gamma_lv cos theta, balancing the three interfacial tensions. Hydrophilic surfaces wet with theta below 90 degrees; polytetrafluoroethylene reaches theta near 110 degrees with water. The Wenzel and Cassie-Baxter models extend Young's equation to rough and chemically heterogeneous surfaces, accounting for the superhydrophobic behaviour observed on lotus leaves and engineered nanostructured coatings.

Pyrimidine carries two nitrogen atoms at the 1- and 3-positions of a six-membered aromatic ring and is strongly deactivated toward electrophiles. The ring forms the core of the nucleobases cytosine, thymine, and uracil, and its electron-poor character allows nucleophilic displacement of leaving groups at the 2-, 4-, and 6-positions in many pharmaceutical syntheses.

Lipinski's rule of five filters orally bioavailable drug candidates by limiting molecular weight to 500 daltons, calculated log P to 5, hydrogen bond donors to 5, and acceptors to 10. Compounds violating two or more criteria have low probability of acceptable absorption. The rules captured statistical regularities of marketed drugs, prompting medicinal chemists to flag and rectify polar surface area or lipophilicity excesses early in lead optimisation.

Standard reduction potentials predict whether a metal will displace another from solution. Zinc, with a potential of minus 0.76 volts, reduces copper ions because copper sits higher in the electrochemical series at plus 0.34 volts. Dropping a zinc strip into copper sulphate deposits copper metal and dissolves zinc, the cell potential of 1.10 volts confirming the spontaneity of the displacement.

Solvolysis of a neopentyl substrate is anomalously slow and gives a rearranged product because the primary carbocation that would form is too unstable. Instead a concerted ionisation with simultaneous methyl migration generates the tertiary cation directly, so the rate-determining step bypasses the primary cation entirely while delivering a tert-amyl product.

For second-row diatomics lighter than oxygen, the 2s and 2p sigma orbitals lie close enough in energy to mix, raising the sigma-2p orbital above the pi-2p pair. This s-p mixing reorders the molecular orbital diagram so that boron and carbon diatomics fill the pi orbitals before the sigma, explaining why B2 is paramagnetic with two unpaired electrons.

London dispersion forces arise from instantaneous fluctuations in electron density that create transient dipoles inducing dipoles in neighbours. Their strength grows with molecular polarisability, which is why the boiling points of the noble gases rise steadily from helium to xenon and why larger hydrocarbons are liquids and waxes while methane is a gas.

The temperature dependence of a reaction enthalpy follows Kirchhoff's law, which states that the rate of change of enthalpy with temperature equals the difference in heat capacity between products and reactants. Integrating this relation lets a reaction enthalpy measured at one temperature be corrected to another, provided the heat capacities are known over the range.

Transition state location proceeds by following the intrinsic reaction coordinate from a saddle point on the potential energy surface, where one eigenvalue of the Hessian is negative and all others positive. Quasi-Newton optimisers such as Berny algorithm step uphill along the negative-curvature mode and downhill along the others. Subsequent IRC calculations verify connection of the saddle to the desired reactant and product minima.

A primary alcohol is oxidised to an aldehyde and then further to a carboxylic acid by chromium-based reagents in aqueous acid. To stop cleanly at the aldehyde, a milder anhydrous oxidant such as pyridinium chlorochromate is used, since it lacks the water needed to form the hydrate that the chromium would otherwise oxidise onward to the acid.

Miller indices label crystal planes by the reciprocals of their fractional intercepts with the unit cell axes, cleared of fractions. The (111) plane in a cubic crystal intercepts all three axes equally, while (100) is parallel to two axes. The interplanar spacing for a cubic lattice follows 1 over d squared equal to (h squared plus k squared plus l squared) divided by the lattice parameter squared.

The Chapman mechanism describes stratospheric ozone steady state through O2 photolysis at wavelengths below 240 nanometres, atom-molecule combination forming ozone, ozone photolysis at 240 to 320 nanometres regenerating atoms, and atom-ozone recombination back to two O2 molecules. Catalytic destruction by ClO and BrO radicals from anthropogenic halocarbons shifts the steady state and produces the seasonal Antarctic ozone hole.

Gelatinisation of starch granules in water occurs around 60 to 75 degrees Celsius as hydrogen bonds between amylopectin chains break and water swells the crystalline regions. Above the gelatinisation temperature the granules disrupt and amylose leaches into the surrounding solution, increasing viscosity. On cooling, the amylose chains retrograde into double helices that crystallise slowly, causing staling of bread and syneresis from starch gels.

Conjugation lowers the energy of a pi system by letting electron density spread over adjacent p orbitals. In 1,3-butadiene both the s-cis and s-trans conformers retain conjugation, and the central carbon-carbon single bond is shorter than an ordinary single bond because of the partial double-bond character contributed by the delocalised framework.

The common ion effect suppresses solubility when one of the ions of a sparingly soluble salt is already present. Silver chloride is far less soluble in dilute sodium chloride than in pure water, because the elevated chloride concentration forces the equilibrium back toward the solid in accordance with the fixed value of the solubility product.

Infrared spectroscopy probes molecular vibrations whose frequencies depend on bond strength and reduced mass. The carbonyl stretch of esters appears near 1735 cm^-1, ketones near 1715, and amides near 1650, while broad O-H stretches at 3200-3550 distinguish alcohols and acids. Fingerprint region absorptions below 1500 cm^-1 are highly specific to individual compounds.

Scanning tunnelling microscopy resolves individual atoms on conducting surfaces by exploiting the exponential dependence of tunnelling current on tip-sample separation, I proportional to exp(-2 kappa z) with kappa around 10 inverse nanometres for typical work functions. Atomic resolution is achieved because the current is dominated by the apex atom of the tip. STM also enables single-molecule manipulation, demonstrated by Eigler's spelling of IBM with 35 xenon atoms.

Shape-memory alloys such as nitinol exploit a reversible martensitic transformation between austenite and martensite phases triggered by temperature or stress. Deformation in the low-temperature martensite phase is recovered on heating above the austenite finish temperature as the lattice reverts to its high-symmetry parent structure. Pseudoelastic recovery at body temperature underpins applications in stents and orthodontic archwires.

Structure-based drug design uses crystal structures of target proteins to position inhibitors that fill specific pockets. The HIV protease inhibitors saquinavir, ritonavir, and the subsequent generation of darunavir all carry transition-state mimetic hydroxyethylamine or hydroxyethylene cores that occupy the catalytic dyad. Backbone hydrogen-bonding patterns rather than side-chain contacts give darunavir its retention of potency against resistance mutations that escape earlier drugs.

Triplet-triplet annihilation upconversion combines a sensitiser that absorbs low-energy photons and intersystem-crosses to its triplet state with an annihilator whose triplet state lies at half the energy of its singlet. Two annihilator triplets fuse to one singlet that emits at higher energy than was absorbed. Platinum octaethylporphyrin sensitiser paired with diphenylanthracene annihilator converts green light to blue with overall yields up to 30 percent.

Chemiluminescence of luminol in alkaline aqueous solution requires hydrogen peroxide and a catalyst such as ferricyanide or hemin. The diazaquinone intermediate releases nitrogen and forms an electronically excited aminophthalate dianion that relaxes to its ground state with emission at 425 nanometres. Forensic blood detection exploits the catalytic activity of heme iron in haemoglobin to give the characteristic blue glow.

Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances earn the name forever chemicals because their carbon-fluorine bonds resist hydrolysis, photolysis, and biological degradation. Perfluorooctanoic acid was detected in serum of essentially all sampled Americans by 2005, with environmental concentrations above the recently revised EPA drinking water health advisory of 0.004 parts per trillion. Atmospheric oxidation of fluorotelomer alcohols produces perfluorocarboxylic acids that deposit globally including in remote Arctic ecosystems.

In a reaction limited by a slow first step followed by a fast step, the rate-determining step alone fixes the observed rate law. For the reaction of nitrogen dioxide with carbon monoxide, the bimolecular step 2 NO2 giving NO plus NO3 is slow, so the rate is second order in NO2 and zero order in carbon monoxide despite carbon monoxide appearing in the overall stoichiometry.

A bomb calorimeter measures the heat of combustion at constant volume by igniting a sample in excess oxygen inside a sealed steel vessel immersed in water. The temperature rise of the water and the calorimeter, multiplied by the heat capacity of the assembly, gives the internal energy change, which is converted to enthalpy by adding the work term for the change in moles of gas.

The chemical shift of a proton reflects the local electron density that shields it from the applied field. Protons near electronegative atoms or in the deshielding cone of an aromatic ring resonate downfield; aromatic protons appear near 7 ppm and aldehyde protons near 10 ppm, while shielded protons on saturated carbons cluster between 0.5 and 2 ppm.

Henry's law states that the partial pressure of a solute gas above a dilute solution is proportional to its mole fraction in solution, P = K_H x. The proportionality constant K_H depends on temperature and solute identity. The law governs the dissolution of atmospheric gases in water and the carbonation of beverages, where loss of pressure leads to CO2 outgassing.

Radiocarbon dating exploits the steady production of carbon-14 in the atmosphere and its uptake by living organisms. When an organism dies it stops exchanging carbon, and the carbon-14 decays with a half-life of 5730 years. Measuring the residual carbon-14 to carbon-12 ratio and applying the exponential decay law yields an age accurate over roughly fifty thousand years.

Aromatic electrophilic substitution proceeds through a Wheland intermediate or arenium ion, formed when an electrophile attacks the aromatic ring. Loss of the ipso proton restores aromaticity and regenerates a substituted arene. Electron-donating substituents activate the ring and direct ortho or para, while electron-withdrawing groups deactivate and direct meta.

The triple bond of ethyne involves sp hybridised carbons whose two sp orbitals lie 180 degrees apart, making the molecule linear. The remaining two p orbitals on each carbon form two mutually perpendicular pi bonds. The high s character of the sp orbitals draws bonding electrons closer to carbon, making the carbon-hydrogen bond acidic enough to be deprotonated by strong base.

The Grunwald-Winstein equation correlates solvolysis rates with solvent ionising power through a linear free-energy relationship. The logarithm of the rate ratio relative to a standard solvent equals a substrate-specific sensitivity parameter multiplied by the solvent ionising power, and the slope reveals how much positive charge develops in the rate-determining step.

The Maxwell-Boltzmann speed distribution describes the spread of molecular speeds in a gas at thermal equilibrium. The curve rises from zero, peaks at the most probable speed, and tails off at high speed. Raising the temperature broadens and flattens the distribution and shifts the peak to higher speed, increasing the fraction of molecules energetic enough to surmount a reaction barrier.

Capsaicin in chilli peppers binds the TRPV1 ion channel on sensory neurons, producing the burning sensation conventionally measured in Scoville heat units. Pure capsaicin scores 16 million SHU; habanero peppers reach 350,000. The molecule survives heating to over 200 degrees Celsius without loss of potency, hence the persistence of chilli flavour through cooking, and its bioavailability through fat dissolution explains why dairy soothes a chilli burn better than water.

Vulcanisation of natural rubber by sulphur introduces polysulphide cross-links between adjacent polyisoprene chains, converting the soft tacky elastomer into a tough material with reversible elasticity. The number of sulphur atoms in each bridge ranges from one to eight depending on cure conditions, and accelerators such as benzothiazole derivatives shift the distribution toward shorter bridges that give better thermal and oxidative ageing performance.

Cis-trans isomerisation of azobenzene proceeds upon UV irradiation around 365 nanometres, populating the n-pi-star excited state from which the molecule relaxes either to the cis isomer or back to the more stable trans form. Visible light at 450 nanometres drives the reverse cis-to-trans conversion through the pi-pi-star band. The thermal half-life of cis-azobenzene at room temperature ranges from hours to days depending on substitution.

Nitrogen runoff from agricultural fertiliser enters waterways largely as nitrate. In eutrophic estuaries the excess nitrogen stimulates phytoplankton blooms whose decomposition consumes oxygen, producing hypoxic dead zones. The Gulf of Mexico dead zone fed by Mississippi River discharge varies between 5,000 and 20,000 square kilometres annually, with denitrification in shelf sediments releasing the nitrogen as N2 but also as the powerful greenhouse gas N2O.

Antiaromatic rings carrying 4n pi electrons are destabilised relative to an open-chain reference. Cyclobutadiene with four pi electrons is so unstable that it dimerises rapidly even at low temperature, and it distorts to a rectangular geometry that breaks the degeneracy of its highest occupied orbitals to avoid an open-shell triplet.

Karl Fischer titration determines trace water through the reaction of iodine, sulphur dioxide, a base, and an alcohol, in which water is consumed stoichiometrically with iodine. In the coulometric variant the iodine is generated electrochemically, and the charge passed measures the iodine produced, allowing water contents down to a few parts per million to be quantified precisely.

The Wagner-Meerwein rearrangement is a 1,2-shift of an alkyl or aryl group within a carbocation, central to the chemistry of bicyclic terpenes. The rearrangement of the bornyl cation to the camphene framework proceeds through skeletal reorganisation, and the strained ring systems of natural monoterpenes provide ample thermodynamic driving force for such migrations.

The heat capacity of a calorimeter is found by a calibration run in which a known quantity of heat, often supplied electrically or by burning a standard such as benzoic acid, raises the temperature by a measured amount. Dividing the known heat by the temperature rise gives the calorimeter constant used to interpret subsequent measurements.

Ammonia, water, and hydrogen fluoride show anomalously high boiling points among the hydrides of their groups because hydrogen bonding links the molecules through the lone pairs of the electronegative central atom. The hydrides of the heavier congeners lack this association and follow the expected trend of rising boiling point with molar mass.

The Hartree-Fock method approximates the many-electron wavefunction as a single Slater determinant of one-electron orbitals optimised self-consistently in the mean field of the other electrons. The Fock matrix F = H_core + 2J - K combines core, Coulomb, and exchange contributions; diagonalisation yields molecular orbital energies. The variational principle guarantees that the HF energy bounds the true ground state from above, and the missing correlation energy defines the post-HF target.

The solubility of many metal sulphides is strongly pH dependent because sulphide is the conjugate base of a weak acid. In acidic solution the low sulphide concentration keeps zinc sulphide dissolved while the far less soluble copper sulphide still precipitates, allowing the two metals to be separated by controlling pH in the classical qualitative analysis scheme.

The Fischer projection draws a sugar with the carbon chain vertical and the carbonyl at the top. Horizontal bonds point toward the viewer and vertical bonds away. A D sugar has the hydroxyl on the highest-numbered stereocentre pointing right, and the assignment is made by reference to D-glyceraldehyde, the configurational standard from which the entire sugar family is derived.

Alpha decay emits a helium nucleus, lowering the mass number by four and the atomic number by two. Uranium-238 decaying to thorium-234 is a classic example. The emitted alpha particle carries a discrete energy because the decay connects two definite nuclear states, and its short range in matter makes it dangerous only when an alpha emitter is ingested or inhaled.

Pincer ligands enforce mer coordination of three donor atoms in a planar arrangement around a metal centre, leaving two trans coordination sites available for catalytic chemistry. PCP, NCN, and PNP pincers stabilise unusual oxidation states and intermediates, allowing isolation of d8 Rh(III)-H species, multiply bonded Ir nitrenes, and Fe complexes that activate dinitrogen at ambient pressure.

An HSQC experiment correlates each proton with the carbon to which it is directly bonded, producing a single cross-peak per carbon-hydrogen pair. Overlapping proton signals that defy assignment in one dimension separate cleanly when spread against the wider carbon dispersion, making HSQC indispensable for unravelling crowded spectra of complex natural products.

Nucleophilic acyl substitution proceeds through addition of a nucleophile to the carbonyl carbon to give a tetrahedral intermediate, followed by expulsion of the leaving group to restore the carbonyl. The net result is replacement of one group at the acyl carbon, distinguishing the reaction from the simple addition seen with aldehydes and ketones.

Free radical polymerisation of styrene proceeds through initiation by thermal decomposition of benzoyl peroxide into phenyl radicals, propagation by repeated addition of styrene monomer to the growing chain end, and termination by combination or disproportionation. The kinetic chain length is proportional to [M]/[I]^{1/2}, and chain transfer to solvent or monomer caps the achievable molecular weight. Polydispersity indices near 2.0 are characteristic of this statistical process.

subtopic: peptide bond formation and protecting groups
sentence: Benzyl ethers and esters protect hydroxyl and carboxyl groups and are cleaved by catalytic hydrogenolysis over palladium, which cleaves the benzylic carbon-oxygen bond and releases toluene. Because hydrogenolysis proceeds under neutral conditions, the benzyl group is orthogonal to acid- and base-labile protectors and survives both acidic and basic deprotection steps.

A Frost diagram plots the product of oxidation state and standard potential against oxidation state, so the slope between two points gives the potential of the corresponding couple. A species lying above the line joining its neighbours is thermodynamically poised to disproportionate, while one lying below is the stable product of comproportionation, making the diagram a compact map of redox stability.

A radioactive tracer is an isotope substituted into a molecule so that its progress can be followed by the radiation it emits. Phosphorus-32 incorporated into a nucleotide tags it without altering its chemistry, and gamma-emitting technetium-99m introduced into the body localises in tissues of interest, the workhorse of diagnostic nuclear medicine imaging.

Pyridine undergoes electrophilic substitution sluggishly and at the 3-position because the electronegative nitrogen withdraws electron density and destabilises the intermediates leading to 2- and 4-substitution. Nucleophilic substitution, by contrast, occurs readily at the 2- and 4-positions, where the developing negative charge is stabilised on nitrogen.

The cage effect describes how solvent molecules surround a pair of freshly formed radicals and hold them together long enough for some to recombine before they can diffuse apart. A more viscous solvent strengthens the cage, raising the fraction of geminate recombination and lowering the yield of free radicals available for productive chain chemistry.

Mutarotation of glucose is observed as a change in optical rotation when freshly dissolved crystals reach equilibrium. Pure alpha-glucose starts at plus 112 degrees and pure beta-glucose at plus 19 degrees, and both drift to the equilibrium value of plus 52.7 degrees, corresponding to a mixture of roughly 36 percent alpha and 64 percent beta, with a trace of the open-chain form.

Silicon and carbon differ sharply despite sharing group 14. Carbon forms strong pi bonds and exists as carbon dioxide, a discrete molecule with carbon-oxygen double bonds, whereas silicon forms weak pi bonds and instead builds silicon dioxide as an extended covalent network of corner-sharing tetrahedra, which is why quartz is a hard high-melting solid and carbon dioxide a gas.

The Fenton reaction generates hydroxyl radicals when ferrous iron reduces hydrogen peroxide, the iron being oxidised to the ferric state. The highly reactive radical attacks organic substrates indiscriminately. Cycling the iron back to the plus two state with a co-reductant sustains the catalysis, the basis of advanced oxidation processes for destroying recalcitrant pollutants in wastewater.

The halogens grade smoothly in physical state from gaseous fluorine and chlorine through liquid bromine to solid iodine as dispersion forces strengthen with increasing electron count. Their oxidising power falls down the group, so chlorine displaces bromide and iodide from solution while iodine cannot displace the lighter halides, a reactivity order confirmed by standard electrode potentials.

Cross-conjugation occurs when three unsaturated groups branch from a central atom so that conjugation extends along any two paths but never all three at once. Divinyl ketone exemplifies the pattern, and the electronic communication between its two vinyl groups is attenuated relative to a linearly conjugated dienone, altering both ultraviolet absorption and reactivity.

In ethene each carbon is sp2 hybridised, with three trigonal-planar sigma bonds and one unhybridised p orbital. The two p orbitals overlap sideways to form the pi bond, which lies above and below the molecular plane. Rotation about the double bond would break this pi overlap, accounting for the high barrier that locks alkene geometry into cis or trans.

The solubility product of silver chloride is 1.8e-10 at 25 degrees Celsius, so in pure water the molar solubility is the square root of that value, about 1.3e-5 moles per litre. Both ion concentrations equal this figure, and any combination of silver and chloride concentrations whose product exceeds the solubility product will precipitate solid silver chloride.

Epimers are sugars that differ in configuration at a single stereocentre. Glucose and galactose are C4 epimers, while glucose and mannose are C2 epimers. The Lobry de Bruyn-Alberda van Ekenstein rearrangement interconverts glucose, mannose, and fructose under mild base through a common enediol intermediate, scrambling the configuration at C2 and shifting the carbonyl between C1 and C2.

Across a period the oxides change from basic through amphoteric to acidic as the elements become more electronegative. Sodium oxide dissolves in water to give a strong alkali, aluminium oxide reacts with both acids and bases, and sulphur trioxide dissolves to give sulphuric acid, the trend mirroring the shift from ionic metal oxides to covalent non-metal oxides.

Metal-organic frameworks combine inorganic secondary building units with multitopic organic linkers to give crystalline porous solids. MOF-5, built from Zn4O clusters bridged by 1,4-benzenedicarboxylate, possesses internal surface area above 3000 square metres per gram and pore apertures near 0.8 nanometres. Reticular synthesis using isoreticular linkers extends the same topology to larger pores, tunable hydrophobicity, and selective gas adsorption.

Coupling constants carry geometric information through the Karplus relationship, which expresses the three-bond proton-proton coupling as a function of the dihedral angle. Couplings near 8 to 12 hertz indicate dihedral angles close to 0 or 180 degrees, while couplings near 2 to 4 hertz correspond to angles near 90 degrees, allowing ring conformations to be deduced from the spectrum.

Prodrug strategies mask polar or labile functionality with cleavable promoieties to improve absorption or distribution. Enalapril is the ethyl ester prodrug of enalaprilat, hydrolysed by hepatic carboxylesterases to expose the carboxylate that chelates the active-site zinc of angiotensin-converting enzyme. The strategy raises oral bioavailability from 25 percent for the parent diacid to 60 percent for the ester.

The enthalpy of neutralisation of a strong acid by a strong base is nearly constant at about minus 57 kilojoules per mole because the net reaction is always the formation of water from hydronium and hydroxide ions. Weak acids give smaller magnitudes because energy is absorbed to complete their dissociation before neutralisation.

The steady-state approximation sets the net rate of change of a reactive intermediate to zero, allowing its concentration to be expressed in terms of stable species. Applied to the Lindemann mechanism for unimolecular decomposition, it predicts a rate that is second order at low pressure, where activating collisions are scarce, and first order at high pressure, where activation is fast.

Saponification hydrolyses an ester under basic conditions to a carboxylate salt and an alcohol. Hydroxide adds to the carbonyl, the tetrahedral intermediate ejects the alkoxide, and the resulting carboxylic acid is immediately deprotonated by the alkoxide. This final irreversible deprotonation makes basic hydrolysis effectively one-way, unlike the reversible acid-catalysed reaction.

The chlor-alkali process electrolyses brine in membrane cells to produce chlorine at a titanium anode coated with mixed ruthenium and iridium oxides while hydrogen evolves at a nickel cathode. The cation-exchange membrane allows Na+ to migrate but rejects hydroxide, keeping the caustic compartment free of chloride. The combined energy demand approaches 2.2 megawatt-hours per tonne of chlorine produced, dominated by the kinetic overpotential at both electrodes.

Hydrofluorination of an alkyne with a gold catalyst adds hydrogen and fluorine across the triple bond to give a vinyl fluoride. The metal activates the alkyne toward attack by a fluoride source, and the regiochemistry follows Markovnikov selectivity, placing the fluorine on the more substituted carbon of the resulting alkene.

Egg white proteins denature on whisking through mechanical shear and air-water interface exposure. Ovalbumin and conalbumin unfold, exposing hydrophobic patches that aggregate around incorporated air bubbles to stabilise the foam. Cream of tartar lowers pH toward the isoelectric point of ovalbumin near 4.5, reducing electrostatic repulsion and tightening the protein network so the meringue holds its structure during baking without collapsing.

Formal charge is assigned by giving each atom its non-bonding electrons plus half the bonding electrons, then subtracting from the free-atom valence count. Among resonance structures the one with formal charges closest to zero, and any negative charge on the most electronegative atom, is the largest contributor to the resonance hybrid.

A stereocentre bearing four different substituents is assigned R or S by ranking the substituents by Cahn-Ingold-Prelog priority and viewing the molecule with the lowest priority group pointing away. A clockwise descent through the remaining three from highest to lowest priority denotes R, counterclockwise denotes S. The descriptor is independent of the sign of optical rotation.
